Water splitting: The absorbed light energy is used to power a process called photolysis, which splits water molecules into oxygen gas and hydrogen ions.  3. Carbon fixation: The hydrogen ions are used to convert carbon dioxide into a usable form, while the oxygen gas is released as a byproduct.  4. It was formalized after the rebuilding of Athens following the Persian destruction in 480 BCE. The annual Dionysia festival featured competitions in tragedy, comedy, and satyr plays. The theatres had specific features like tall arched entrances called parodoi or eisodoi, a two-story skênê with an episkenion, and sometimes a raised speaking place on the orchestra called the logeion. All tragedies were unique pieces written in honor of Dionysus and played only once until the Hellenistic period. The theatre was used for both public meetings and dramatic performances, with every Greek town having an open-air theatre set in a hillside outside the town. Tragedy and comedy were viewed as completely separate genres with no plays merging aspects of the two.

The conquests led to a steady emigration of young and ambitious Greeks to the new Greek empires in the east, resulting in a process of Hellenization and intermixing in regions that had previously been in contact with Greek colonies.
